styleAnswer.evidence: The office chair is a small navy-blue seat-back with a dark base. It uses roughly 3 lightness steps on the blue body (a flat mid blue, a slightly lighter highlight, and a dark edge), against about 5-6 steps on the references (bench wood, hedge greens, stall and well). It has 12 distinct colours, below the stall (40) and well (38) and similar to the simpler bench (14), hedge (11) and lamp (14). 19% of its pixels sit in 5x5 flat blocks, against 0% for the bench, hedge, lamp and well, so the seat and back read as flat fills with no grain, speckle or per-part shading. Only 30% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans partly to a tinted dark blue, but the dark base and edges look fairly uniform and sticker-like. Compared with the hedge, which packs 10 colours per tile of leaf clumps, or the bench's shaded slats, the chair looks flatter and thinner. Its low density is partly down to the object being small and sparse, but the flat-fill coverage and shallow ramp still make it look weaker next to the references.
